fact: Connecting Africa, citing Djibouti Telecom states the DARE1 submarine cable, operational since 2021 with 36 Tbps over three fibre pairs, links Djibouti City with Bosaso and Mogadishu in Somalia and Mombasa in Kenya.

ITWeb Africa, citing Djibouti Telecom states the DARE1 submarine cable, operational since 2021 with 36 Tbps over three fibre pairs, links Djibouti City with Bosaso and Mogadishu in Somalia and Mombasa in Kenya.
TechAfrica News reports that Djibouti Telecom's DARE1 subsea cable already links Djibouti, Somalia and Kenya; no Somali landing station is named.
DatacenterDynamics lists Somalia's current landings as DARE1 at Mogadishu and Bosaso and Gulf2Africa (G2A) at Bosaso and Berbera, so two cables land at different stations.
DatacenterDynamics reports Hormuud Telecom's newly completed Somali cable landing station (location undisclosed) is open-access and will accommodate various submarine cables.
Vertiv says it completed Hormuud Telecom's new open-access cable landing station in Somalia, which will accommodate various submarine cables and ease cross-connections for local and global partners.

The Star reports Somcable Submarine Network (Somaliland-based) operates two international subsea landings, 2Africa and PEACE, at the Port of Berbera, which its CTO calls two physically diverse routes.

A Somali Ministry of Information adviser writing in a personal capacity says five submarine cables land on the Somali coast; no cable names or landing stations given, and no date given so the 2026-08-19 publication date is used.
Developing Telecoms, citing Ecofin, says Somalia has an existing connection to five international submarine cables; none named, and the article date is used as no other is given.
Bloomberg reports four submarine cables land on Somalia's coast, two co-financed by Hormuud; landing stations and independence not stated.
